Python reference: fine-tuning

Source: vignettes/articles/python-fine-tuning.Rmd
python-fine-tuning.Rmd

New heads for your own targets on the encoder of a trained model, a checkpoint or a member of a suite, and the fine-tuned models released as a suite of their own. Fine-tuning a trained model runs every name below on the survey that ships with the R package.

ParentModel 

ParentModel.open(source, config=InitFromConfig())

The trained model a fine-tuned model starts from, its parent. source is a checkpoint, or a suite directory whose member config.suite_target and config.suite_seed name; a suite member’s size and SHA-256 are checked against the manifest before it is read. A checkpoint that carries no species vocabulary, only its size, is refused.

  • vocabs() (ExternalVocabs) and dataset_config() (DatasetConfig): what the fine-tuning plots are loaded with, so each species is read through the row of the embedding table the parent gives it. The vocabularies also replay the classes of a target the parent shares.
  • model_config (ModelConfig): the configuration the fine-tuned model takes. Only the fields in FINE_TUNE_MODEL_FIELDS may be changed.
  • schema (ResolveSchema), scalers (Scalers) and categorical_vocab (CategoricalVocab): the parent’s.
  • record (ParentRecord): what a fine-tuned checkpoint keeps of it; reuse, n_tensors and heads are set by Trainer.init_from.
config = rc.InitFromConfig()
config.suite_target, config.suite_seed = "habitat", 1
parent = rc.ParentModel.open(suite_dir, config)
plots = rc.ResolveDataset.from_pandas(header, species, roles, targets,
                                     config=parent.dataset_config(), vocabs=parent.vocabs())
model_config = parent.model_config
model_config.freeze_encoder = True
trainer = rc.Trainer(rc.ResolveModel(plots.schema,
                                     rc.model_config_for_dataset(plots, model_config)),
                     rc.TrainConfig())
trainer.init_from(parent)

InitFromConfig

Where a warm start reads its parent from and what it carries over.

  • reuse (InitReuse, default Encoder): read by Trainer.init_from.
  • suite_target (str): with a suite directory, the target whose member to start from; may stay empty for a suite of one target.
  • suite_seed (int, default -1): that member’s seed; -1 takes the target’s first member.

InitReuse

What Trainer.init_from carries over besides every parameter and buffer outside the task heads: Encoder (every head starts fresh) or EncoderHeads (also the head of each target the parent shares under the same name, task, transform and classes, with its target scaler). In a config they are spelled encoder and encoder_heads.

ParentRecord

The parent a fine-tuned checkpoint records (RunMetadata.parent, Trainer.parent).

  • checkpoint (str), sha256 (str, lower-case hex) and bytes (int): the parent file as opened.
  • resolve_version (str): the engine that trained the parent.
  • reuse (InitReuse), n_tensors (int, the parameters and buffers copied) and heads (list[str], the parent heads carried over).
  • suite, suite_target (str) and suite_seed (int): the suite member it came from; suite is empty for a checkpoint opened directly. licence and training_scope (str): that suite’s terms.

fine_tune_mismatches() 

fine_tune_mismatches(parent, model_config, schema)

Every way a fine-tuned model’s config and data schema depart from what its parent fixes, as messages: an encoder-shaping config field with another value, other loader settings, other vocabularies, covariates, categorical columns, coordinates, taxonomy or abundance. Empty when the model reads the plots as its parent does. Trainer.init_from raises ValueError listing them.

FINE_TUNE_MODEL_FIELDS

The ModelConfig fields a fine-tuned model may set apart from its parent’s: the heads (head_hidden_dims, head_activation, head_dropout), the dropout rates and what is frozen (freeze_composition, freeze_encoder).

write_derived_suite() 

write_derived_suite(dir, spec)

Releases fine-tuned checkpoints as a suite in dir, which must not hold a manifest yet. Each member is copied to members/<target>/seed_<seed>.pt; the manifest takes its input contract from the parent suite (the part of it the targets’ members read), names for each target the parent suite and target its members started from (SuiteTarget.derived_from) and per member the SHA-256 of its parent checkpoint (SuiteMember.parent_sha256), and lists a vote’s classes. The manifest is sealed and the suite loaded once, so every member is checked against it. Returns the SuiteManifest. A member that records no parent, one started from another suite or from a checkpoint that is not the parent suite’s member of the seed it records, and members of one target started from different parent targets raise ValueError.

DerivedSuiteSpec

The suite write_derived_suite writes: parent (the directory of the suite the members started from), name, description, licence, training_scope (the plots the fine-tuned members were trained on) and targets (list[DerivedSuiteTarget]).

DerivedSuiteTarget

One target of a derived suite: name, members (list[DerivedSuiteMember]), and optionally outputs (the heads read; empty reads the head named name), combine (SuiteCombine or None: a vote for a classification head, a mean for a regression head), period, units, status, limit, training and validation.

DerivedSuiteMember 

DerivedSuiteMember(checkpoint, seed)

One fine-tuned checkpoint of a derived target and its seed.
